clue.text: Badenoch waits to form this

indicators.note: to form something is to build it out of materials, so the preceding letters are reassembled into a new order

parts.note: all thirteen letters of the leader's surname and the verb are used

explanation.surface: The leader of the Opposition is biding her time before assembling her team.
explanation.walkthrough: Kemi Badenoch leads the UK Conservative Party, in opposition since 2024, so the whole clue is both the anagram and the description of the team she picks.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition leader appoints a team of spokespeople who mirror government ministers; in Britain that team is called by this name.

clue.text: The rain flustered lock keeper

indicators.note: someone flustered is thrown into confusion, so the letters before it are thrown out of order

parts.note: both words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A lock-keeper on a canal is bothered by the downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock keeper' reads as the canal official, but the lock is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fine mesh worn over the head to hold the hair, a lock being a tress of hair, in place.

clue.text: Shrinks like breaking laws

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart, so these letters are split and rearranged

parts.note: as is a synonym of like, as in 'as good as new'
decrees are official orders with the force of law

explanation.surface: Something gets smaller in the same way that crime shrinks respect for the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink is to become smaller, and the verb here is a direct synonym, both being third person singular.

clue.text: Auditor's considered move offshore?

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a listener, so the word is taken as heard rather than as written

parts.note: weighed means considered, as in weighed up the options

explanation.surface: An accountant's careful decision to relocate a business to a tax haven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' and 'offshore' conjure a financial scheme; the auditor is just a listener, and offshore is literally away from the beach into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking out from the beach through shallow water is a literal move off the shore; the question mark flags the pun on tax havens.

clue.text: An awfully nice aunt, say

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the following letters come out badly jumbled

parts.note: the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a relative as a really lovely aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like the casual 'for example', but it is the definition, a verb at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce or proclaim words is to utter them, a formal synonym of the verb say.

clue.text: I almost directed TV show from Asian country

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
to run a business is to direct it
QI is a long-running BBC television quiz panel show

explanation.surface: Someone nearly directed a television programme set in an Asian land.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for someone or something belonging to the nation whose capital is Baghdad, in western Asia.

clue.text: Exile making one a politician, for instance

indicators.note: making one thing into another turns it into something else, so a letter is swapped for new ones

parts.note: the starting word, taken as written
the Roman numeral for one, the letter that is replaced
A as written plus MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Banishment turns someone into a politician, as one case shows.
explanation.walkthrough: EXILE has its I changed into A MP.
explanation.definitionFit: 'For instance' introduces a case illustrating a general point, which is exactly what this word means.

clue.text: Doctor treats men with chat in surgeries

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: both words used letter for letter
'with' adds the next word to the fodder

explanation.surface: A GP sees male patients and chats with them during consultations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'surgeries' paint a GP's practice; the doctor is a verb meaning tamper with, and the surgeries are operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Operations to join a severed limb or tissue back onto the body are examples of surgery, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Snack unsuitable for soldiers

parts.note: surface reading: a light bite that military rations would not include
setter's reading: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a runny yolk, which this firm snack cannot take

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are thin fingers of toast for dipping in a soft-boiled egg; a firm-yolked one leaves them nothing to dip into.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cooked until the yolk is solid is a common snack, and its solid yolk is useless for dipping toast fingers.

clue.text: Cable, inspired by Davey, perhaps did show

indicators.note: to be inspired is literally to be breathed into, so one name goes inside the other

parts.note: Ed Davey, leader of the Liberal Democrats; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of an Ed
Vince Cable, a former Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: One Lib Dem leader, taking his cue from another, put on a display.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable and Ed Davey are successive Liberal Democrat leaders; Cable sits inside Davey's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To display a quality or feeling clearly is to show it, and the past tense matches 'did show'.

clue.text: Half of army once more retreats and falls

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction
half of a word means only its front portion is kept

parts.note: the first two of its four letters
again means once more

explanation.surface: An army attacks again, then half of it pulls back and is beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: AR plus AGAIN is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border are a proper-name example of falls.

clue.text: In a cryptic crossword, gets hints

indicators.note: a cryptic crossword is where words routinely get scrambled, so these letters appear in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver remarks that a cryptic puzzle gives you clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hints' look like the clues themselves, but the word means traces, as in faint touches of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour or quality, so hints and tinges are synonyms as plural nouns.

clue.text: Group of countries raced, having dropped like flies?

parts.note: the United Nations
to zip is to move very fast

explanation.surface: Nations sprinted and then collapsed in large numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped like flies' suggests mass collapse; here the flies are trouser flies, and these have been undone.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouser flies close with a fastener; opening it lets them fall open, so the past participle fits the pun.

clue.text: Raced, lapping second, and made a splash

indicators.note: lapping means wrapping round, as a runner laps a slower one, so one word encircles the other

parts.note: sped means raced
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A racer overtook the runner in second place and made a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' wants to be S; it is the latter of two.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter liquid in drops all over something is to splash it, a direct past-tense synonym.

clue.text: They clean larks around start of month

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: larks are pranks or capers
the first of September, written as Roman one plus the month's abbreviation

explanation.surface: Cleaners fooling about at the beginning of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: The month's start is read as 1 Sept, the first day of September with I as the Roman one. Larks here are capers, not birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Substances applied to wounds or surfaces to kill germs are cleansers, so 'they clean' stands for the plural noun.

clue.text: Revolutionary ways to collar boxer in upset

indicators.note: to collar someone is to grab them round the neck, so the outer pieces hold the inner ones

parts.note: two ways, each ST for street, split to wrap round the middle
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Roads are closed off to detain a fighter during a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' at the start looks like a reversal signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Soviet leader's hardline communism, so an adjective or noun for that kind of revolutionary.

clue.text: First person in The Aeneid, for example, to get close to Dido

parts.note: e.g., the abbreviation of exempli gratia; the backwards run in 'to get' is a coincidence, not a hiding place

indicators.note: the close of something is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the queen's name

explanation.surface: A reader wonders who in Virgil's epic first approaches Queen Dido.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' suggests the first character on stage, but it is grammar: the Latin for 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil wrote in Latin, where the first-person singular pronoun 'I' is this word.

clue.text: Cut The Wrong Trousers

indicators.note: to trouser something is to pocket it, so the phrase keeps the letters inside it

parts.note: found across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A film buff's terse verdict on the Wallace and Gromit film The Wrong Trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wrong Trousers is an Aardman animated short; the title's last word is the hiding verb, meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop or cut with an axe or blade is a direct synonym, both being verbs.

clue.text: Stranger set up call with Starmer, say, after internal reshuffle

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a caw is a crow's call

indicators.note: a reshuffle reorders a team, and internal limits it to the inner letters of the name

parts.note: Keir Starmer, the UK Prime Minister; 'say' marks him as one Keir

explanation.surface: A strange political plan: arrange a phone call with the Prime Minister after a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Keir's middle two letters swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger here is the comparative adjective, more odd, and this word means more eccentric or zany.

clue.text: Code for one not quite in the habit of business

definitions.text: Code for one not quite in the habit of business

parts.words: Code for one not quite in the habit of business
parts.note: surface reading: rules for someone not fully used to the ways of commerce
setter's reading: a habit is clothing, so the code is a dress code a notch below a business suit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' means custom on the surface but clothing here, as in a nun's habit; 'code' is a dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress code asking for neat but not formal clothes, between business attire and everyday wear.

clue.text: I'm not sure about that false Messiah from part of Italy

parts.note: the hesitant noise of someone unsure
Brian, mistaken for the Messiah in Monty Python's Life of Brian

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts the claims of a fake saviour from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Monty Python film Life of Brian, Brian is hailed as the Messiah against his will.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a landlocked region of central Italy, and the adjective describes someone or something from there.

clue.text: Unearth old note about wine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first pair of words wraps round the last

parts.note: ex means former
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
cava is a Spanish sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Dig up an old tasting note about a wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old note' is read as one unit that goes round the wine: the two short pieces sit on either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it out of the ground, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Some have no money, leaving bit of a sting

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters are taken from within the phrase

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Some people are broke, being on the end of a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' suggests a con that leaves you penniless; here it is an insect's sting.
explanation.definitionFit: The poison injected by a wasp or scorpion is the harmful part of its sting.

clue.text: Sailor's wrong in a couple of ways

parts.note: a sin is a wrong, one way of reading the word
a second way of reading wrong: bad

explanation.surface: A seaman has made two mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong in a couple of ways' asks for two words for wrong placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary seafarer of the Arabian Nights voyages is the archetypal storybook sailor.

clue.text: Rave is focus for Sabrina Carpenter, perhaps

indicators.note: the focus of something is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters
the carpenter ant is a kind of ant that tunnels into wood

explanation.surface: A dance party is the main interest of the pop singer Sabrina Carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: The pop star's name is split: her first name supplies a letter and her surname is the wood-boring insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to talk wildly and angrily, so this verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Pub in that place not wholly solvent

indicators.note: not wholly means incomplete, so the word drops its final letter

parts.note: there means in that place
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub nearby is not entirely in the black financially.
explanation.walkthrough: THERE loses its last letter to THER and holds INN. 'Solvent' suggests being able to pay debts; it is a liquid that dissolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid used to dilute paint or dissolve grease, such as white spirit, is a solvent.

clue.text: Constant suffering

definitions.meaning: second meaning: tolerating, putting up with

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like chronic pain; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lasting, as in an abiding memory, and also tolerating, from to abide something.

clue.text: Planning ahead, clean up inside before sex

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: inside means within, so the first phrase sits within the next piece

parts.note: mating is sexual coupling
to edit is to tidy a text

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up in advance of a romantic encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' sends the tidying word into the word for sex, just after its first letter, not into the prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotting something in advance is what this present participle means, as in a premeditated crime.
